title: Hidden PowerShell (PID 2976) opens LSASS and winlogon with full-access masks on SCRANTON
rationale: All describe the same event: PowerShell.exe PID 2976 as pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local opening lsass.exe (and winlogon.exe) with GrantedAccess 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff and an UNKNOWN call trace, plus the wsmprovhost.exe LSASS access on NASHUA from the same operator. Full-access handles to LSASS memory are the defining behavior of OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory (T1003.001); the findings' alternate labels (T1056.004, T1212, T1555, T1556, T1558, T1606) describe the same observed action, which is best fit by T1003.001.

title: Masqueraded .scr loader in C:\ProgramData\victim reads LSA registry key and drops steganographic carrier on SCRANTON
rationale: The cod.3aka3.scr loader (launched from explorer.exe, later wiped with sdelete) read HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Lsa, which holds LSA secrets, and dropped monkey.png; sdclt.exe/control.exe UAC-bypass activity is part of the same loader chain. The credential-relevant action is reading the Lsa key, best fit by LSA Secrets (T1003.004); the loader/UAC-bypass steps are the surrounding execution chain.

title: PowerShell screen-capture loop run by pbeesly on SCRANTON
rationale: Invoke-ScreenCapture periodically grabs the full virtual screen via CopyFromScreen and saves .bmp files — GUI input/screen capture, best fit by GUI Input Capture (T1056.002).

title: wsmprovhost.exe (PowerShell Remoting session) opens LSASS with 0x1F3FFF on NASHUA
rationale: not grouped by the consolidation step

title: PowerShell opens Microsoft Edge processes with full access on SCRANTON
rationale: PowerShell PID 2976 opened MicrosoftEdge.exe/MicrosoftEdgeCP.exe/MicrosoftEdgeSH.exe with 0x1FFFFF and an UNKNOWN call trace; full-access handles to a browser process are the prerequisite for reading session cookies, best fit by Steal Web Session Cookie (T1539).

title: accesschk.exe writes passwordsDB and harvested credentials reused via PsExec -p to NASHUA
rationale: accesschk.exe created C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB and PsExec64.exe was then run with the cleartext credential '-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by' against NASHUA. The credential-access action is credentials collected into a file, best fit by Credentials In Files (T1552.001); the PsExec use is the subsequent lateral movement.

title: Registry value HKLM\SOFTWARE\Javasoft 'value Supplement' used as hidden payload store and re-executed via Invoke-Expression
rationale: PowerShell set the registry value to a base64 hidden PowerShell command and later retrieved it with Get-ItemPropertyValue | Invoke-Expression, including a re-execution via hostui.exe runas. Credentials/payload stored and read from the registry is best fit by Credentials in Registry (T1552.002).

title: Get-PrivateKeys exports all LocalMachine certificates to password-protected .pfx files on SCRANTON
rationale: Same script block (readme.ps1, Get-PrivateKeys) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and calling Export-PfxCertificate into Downloads with hardcoded password 'saribas', followed by Invoke-BeachCleanup deleting the .pfx files. Exporting private-key certificates is best fit by Private Keys (T1552.004).

title: Shared MAC 12:34:56:78:9a:bc answering for multiple IPs in Zeek logs
rationale: One L2 address answering for 10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.6 and 192.168.0.4 concurrently is the signature of ARP cache poisoning; F43 confirms no end-to-end AiTM chain beyond this anomaly. Best fit is ARP Cache Poisoning (T1557.002).

title: Root certificate store 'Blob' value modified on NASHUA
rationale: Security 4657 shows the ROOT\Certificates\BE36A456... 'Blob' value modified on nashua.dmevals.local — the only certificate-store modification in the dataset. Tampering with the certificate store is best fit by Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates (T1649).

title: Hidden PowerShell compiles attacker C# with csc.exe into DLLs on SCRANTON
rationale: csc.exe compiling attacker C# into qkbkqqbs.dll and 0piklvia.dll from the hidden PowerShell is tooling execution, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) for the in-memory/compiled payload staging.

title: PyInstaller python.exe pushed via PsExec to NASHUA beacons to 192.168.0.4:8443 and archives credential-named files
rationale: python.exe launched by PSEXESVC as pbeesly opened 348 outbound connections to 192.168.0.4:8443 and spawned PowerShell that enumerated the profile for credential-named files and packed them into a password-protected RAR. The observed action is collection/exfiltration staging and C2, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel).
